arms.label: Ember
evidence: The chain preserves the selected 212 × 155 × 103 mm compact wedge, sloping top, rear plinth, and stable feet.
It specifies the 7-inch landscape touchscreen at about 24° facing the seated operator and explicitly prohibits flipping it.
It accurately places four USB-A plus Ethernet on the right and one USB-C plus two differentiated micro-HDMI sockets rear-high; the correction call reinforces exact identities and counts.
A dedicated cutaway depicts the display, upper plenum, upward-facing Active Cooler, Pi, bottom NVMe and aluminum plate, with split front-to-rear airflow arrows and one exhaust.
The terminal-style 40×13 music UI, five controller keys, and amber light are retained, but the separate recessed power button is omitted.
Seams, captive screws and the internal cutaway provide some boundary information, but the removable bezel, bottom plate, rear hatch, carrier and filter are not identified as removable.
Warm graphite folded aluminum, black PC-ABS, off-white keys, proportions and restrained console identity closely match the design.
The prompts comprehensively prohibit extra USB-C, audio jacks, fake controls, extra fans, blocked grilles, floating ports and exterior PCBs.
Approximate dimensions and presentation-render framing convey limited uncertainty, but the chain omits the design’s explicit unverified-fit and concept-only caveats.
The structured first prompt is highly renderable, and the second call makes narrowly scoped corrections while explicitly preserving the full prior composition.
arms.most_consequential_strength: The cutaway and airflow instructions translate the complete thermal architecture substantially better than the other chains, while the second call corrects critical button and connector errors.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The chain does not clearly visualize the design’s extensive removable service architecture or explicitly state that fit and thermal performance remain unverified.

arms.label: Harbor
evidence: The prompt faithfully specifies the 190 × 165 × 96 mm low wedge, front intake, tall rear leveling heel and level desk stance.
It retains the 7-inch native-landscape screen at about 22° rising toward and facing the seated operator.
Right-side four-USB-A-plus-Ethernet and rear USB-C-plus-two-HDMI-sized openings are clear, with a cable gutter, but the separately accessible display-power USB-C from the written design is absent.

The front intake, single rear 40 mm exhaust and rearward flow are visible, but the Active Cooler, NVMe path and 70/30 split airflow are deliberately excluded with the no-cutaway/no-arrows constraints.
Eight side-rail controller keys, a separate power button, amber LED and tracker-style music UI closely preserve the musician-facing elements.
Although fasteners and material transitions are requested, the removable rear hatch, bottom sled, display cassette and filter are not shown or identified.
Charcoal polymer, bent aluminum, bronze rails, perforated grilles and the restrained console stance accurately reproduce the intended identity and proportions.
Strong negative constraints reject extra side ports, unsupported labels, exposed boards, knobs, faders, speakers, handles, wood, extra fans and implausible geometry.
Approximate sizing and explicit render language provide modest honesty, but the chain does not carry forward the written design’s warning that this is not dimensionally verified CAD.
The single prompt is well organized, visually coherent and feasible, with consistent hero and inset views of one product.
arms.most_consequential_strength: It gives a particularly complete operator-facing presentation, including correct screen relationship, eight controls, power control, status light and connector access.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: By forbidding cutaways and omitting removable-part cues, it leaves the internal cooling stack and service architecture largely untranslated.

arms.label: Quartz
evidence: The chain exactly carries over the compact 132 × 118 × 82 mm wedge, low front, rigid rear heel and level four-foot stance.
It specifies the 4-inch landscape screen, module and active-area proportions, 24° incline, and right-way-up operator-facing interface.
It preserves the rear USB-C, two micro-HDMI and native power actuator plus the right-side four USB-A and Ethernet, with an open-bottom hood and cable-tie feature indicating cable routing.
Two front intake bands, aligned upper/lower channels and one rear 40 mm exhaust are represented, but the Active Cooler and NVMe stack are not directly shown or named.
Five cream controller keys, rear power actuator and an abstract tracker/grid music interface accurately reflect the operator controls.
Visible part lines and captive screws distinguish bezel, shell and base, but the fan hatch, sliding filter, microSD door and removable electronics cassette are not identified.
PC-ABS, folded aluminum, warm-gray grilles, cream keys, accent line and compact proportions closely match the specified visual language.
The prompt explicitly prohibits extra ports, audio jacks, knobs, speakers, exposed boards, transparent shells, unsupported labels and impossible connector geometry.
Approximate overall proportions signal some uncertainty, although specifying exactly 24° hardens a provisional design value and no dimensional-verification caveat is included.
The two-view board is exceptionally specific and renderable, with clear counts, placement, composition, materials and consistency requirements.
arms.most_consequential_strength: It most precisely translates the compact geometry, screen module, controls and complete externally visible connector organization in a coherent two-view instruction.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: It does not visualize the Active Cooler/NVMe thermal stack and only weakly communicates the extensive removable-service scheme.

arms.label: Willow
evidence: The 214 × 158 × 92 mm wedge, 34 mm front, descending rear skirt and level four-foot base accurately match the selected form.
Landscape orientation and the 28° operator-facing slope are preserved, but the prompt does not explicitly retain the 7-inch-class screen size.

The right-side four USB-A plus Ethernet and rear USB-C are correct, but the prompt shows a micro-HDMI opening where the design specifies a panel-extended full-size HDMI service output and omits other service connectors.
Five intake louvers, the display-gap cue and sole rear 40 mm exhaust are present, but the Active Cooler, Pi, NVMe, lower branch and split airflow are not represented.
The eight controller keys and 40×13 tracker-like UI are retained, but the written design’s visually separate ninth power key is omitted by the exactly-eight-buttons constraint.
The prompt provides no clear removable bottom, rear insert, display carrier, Pi/NVMe cassette or filter boundaries.
Graphite metal, charcoal PC-ABS, walnut-toned rails, black glass and compact vintage-inflected console identity are translated very closely.
It strongly prohibits analog jacks, knobs, speakers, duplicate fans, conflicting vents, exposed boards, floating parts, labels and alternate variants.
Approximate proportions and product-design framing provide limited qualification, but the chain omits the design’s explicit unproven-fit, thermal and manufacturability status.
The hero-plus-two-inset composition is clear, consistent and readily renderable despite the fidelity omissions.
arms.most_consequential_strength: Its materials, proportions and graphite/walnut visual identity are cohesive and unusually well specified.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The exact-eight-buttons constraint deletes the separate power control, while the rear video connector type and internal cooling/service architecture diverge from the written design.

comparative_result: Ember ranks first with 35/40 because its multi-call chain uniquely preserves the full internal stack and split airflow while correcting exact connector and button errors. Quartz follows at 34/40 with excellent external fidelity but limited internal/service representation; Harbor scores 32/40; Willow scores 29/40.
disagreements: The closest judgment calls were whether recessed hoods and gutters sufficiently represent cable motion, and whether approximate dimensions alone adequately communicate concept uncertainty. These were credited partially, while explicit internal routing, removable-part labels and unverified-status language received greater weight.
